prompt: After dinner, $\frac{2}{3}$ of a pan of brownies is left. Sam eats $\frac{1}{2}$ of what is left. What fraction of the WHOLE pan did Sam eat?
hint: Sam eats part of a part. The word "of" between two fractions tells you which operation to use.

hints.text: Sam eats part of a part. The word "of" between two fractions tells you which operation to use.
Half of two thirds is $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3}$. Multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, and then simplify the result.
$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$, so Sam ate $\frac{1}{3}$ of the whole pan.

explanation: Sam eats half of the leftover brownies, so the amount is $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3}$ of the pan.
Multiply the numerators and the denominators: $\frac{1 \times 2}{2 \times 3} = \frac{2}{6}$.
Divide the top and bottom of $\frac{2}{6}$ by $2$ to simplify it to $\frac{1}{3}$.
Sam ate $\frac{1}{3}$ of the whole pan.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the pan
steps: Cut the pan into $3$ equal strips; $2$ strips are left.
One strip out of the original $3$ is $\frac{1}{3}$ of the pan.
